answer: Peer review is staked: each grade carries 150 POA at risk, and a 5% spot check re-grades against a second panel. Disagreement dilutes the payout instead of rejecting it. Rewards then vest against future work. The relic of an old review stays visible for six epochs, so a juror's history is readable before it is drawn again. Whether the spot-check rate catches a slow colluder is the open question, and an ocean of small honest grades is exactly where a nectar of quiet collusion would hide.
